name: Ramona Xona Chip Holder 3 well
author: Ramona Optics
part_number: Xona X4 chip holder, 3 slide, SBS footprint
notes:
The three wells of this definition are the three chip pockets of the holder, empty: A1 is the leftmost pocket. NOT A CATALOGUE PLATE. This is a Ramona Optics fixture: an SBS-footprint holder that carries three Xona XonaChip X4 chips (75.50 x 25.50mm, slide format) so that they can be driven as one plate. Xona themselves describe a four-chip arrangement - 'these chips (the size of standard microscope slides) can be combined in a 4-slide plate holder to yield sixteen (16) sample units' - but that is Xona's own tray, not this holder: Ramona's carries three because the pockets are spaced to the MCAM's 18mm micro-camera pitch (see CORRECTION below), and only three 36mm steps fit the SBS footprint. No drawing of the holder exists yet; the #team_vireo thread the request cites discusses making 'a stand-in stand that we make here'. 

REQUESTED, and therefore exact by definition rather than sourced: the 127.76 x 85.48mm ANSI/SLAS footprint with a standard skirt; three rectangular pockets of 25.50 x 75.50mm plus a small clearance, long axis along the plate's width; pocket centres 36mm apart in x at 27.88, 63.88 and 99.88mm, which is twice the MCAM's 18mm micro-camera pitch so every chip sits under the same camera column; and the pocket centre line at y = 42.74mm. Those three x values are symmetric about 63.88mm = 127.76 / 2, and 42.74 = 85.48 / 2, so the block of pockets is centred on the plate, as the request says. GEOMETRY CHECK: the pockets span x 15.13-40.63, 51.13-76.63 and 87.13-112.63mm, leaving a 10.50mm rib between neighbouring pockets and 15.13mm of plate at each end, and y 4.99-80.49mm, leaving 4.99mm at each side. Nothing overruns the footprint. 

CORRECTION, 2026-10-15, applied on this branch before merge. The requester (Slack UT35U0XPX, the originator of the request) followed up: 'The micro-camera pitch is 18 mm, not 9 mm.' The first version of this file followed their original message, which said the MCAM micro-camera pitch was 9mm and therefore put four pockets 27mm apart (3 x 9mm) at x = 23.38, 50.38, 77.38 and 104.38mm. That is superseded: the pitch is 18mm, so the pockets are 36mm apart (2 x 18mm) and three of them fit the SBS footprint instead of four. Both values are recorded here deliberately - the 27mm/9mm figures are what the vendor-independent original request asked for, the 36mm/18mm figures are the corrected instrument geometry, and the corrected ones are what this file implements. There is no vendor drawing of this holder for either value to contradict: it is a Ramona fixture and the requester is the authority on both the holder and the instrument it is aligned to. The correction is self-consistent in a way the original was not: within a chip the four culture units A-D span 3 x 12.00 = 36.00mm, exactly the corrected pocket spacing, so the units line up with the micro-cameras along the plate's length as well as the chips doing so. 

POCKET CLEARANCE: the request says '25.50 x 75.50 mm plus a small clearance' and does not give the clearance, so the pockets are recorded at the chip's nominal 25.50 x 75.50mm and the clearance is left out rather than invented. A machined holder will be slightly larger; the chip can then sit off centre in its pocket by half the clearance, which is the dominant positioning error of this fixture and is NOT captured by any field in this file. 

NOT SPECIFIED BY ANYONE, recorded here as provisional values that must be replaced from the holder's drawing before it is made, and listed as open questions on the request issue: (a) outer_plate_dimensions.height 14.35mm is the ANSI/SLAS 2-2004 microplate height, used because the request says only 'SBS-footprint ... with standard skirt'; (b) the pocket depth, recorded as 1.0mm so that a chip of the inferred 1.0mm thickness sits flush with the holder's top face - it is a consequence of the chip thickness, which Xona does not publish either; (c) the holder's material and colour, left out entirely (no bottom_material, wall_material, bottom_color or wall_color), since the holder may be machined aluminium, 3D printed plastic or acrylic and that decides whether it can be imaged through at all; (d) whether each pocket is a blind pocket or a through-hole, which decides whether the chips can be used on a transmitted-light instrument. The skirt keys are left at the schema's documented defaults, which are the ANSI/SLAS standard skirt the request asked for. The chip that goes in a pocket is Xona_XC-SF150-X4_4_well_plate.json, and the two together are Xona_XC-SF150-X4_in_Ramona_chip_holder_3_well_plate.json, which is the file to use for imaging. CHIP HEIGHT vs PLATE THICKNESS, per the requester's 2026-10-15 follow-up. The 1.00mm figure is kept, still provisional: the requester confirms that the purchasing link in #team_vireo carries no thickness (it is the same plan view already used here), and that Xona's product page, drawings and FAQ give none either, so there is nothing to replace the ISO 8037-1 slide inference with yet. But 1.00mm is the thickness of the flat slide plate ONLY. Xona's product photographs show the O6.0 reservoirs and O2.0 loading ports standing up from that plate as raised bosses, so the chip's overall height is MORE than 1.00mm by an unmeasured amount. Anything that depends on total height rather than on the optical path - pocket depth, lid or tray clearance, a chip sitting flush - must not assume 1.00mm. A caliper measurement of a chip in hand is to follow and will settle both numbers. 

Use 'pitch' and origin reference to compute all well centers.
